transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Um... mostly work stuff. I just... I keep hitting a wall when I have to do any real sitting-down brain work. Like, uh, the monthly reports, or planning these multi-site health events we do. I know it matters, but I just keep putting it off. So... yeah. I figured I should come in.
Do you feel anxious when you think about doing these tasks?
Um... no. Not really. I just... I don't know. I just avoid them. It's not a panic thing.
Do you have trouble focusing or paying attention to details when you're working on tasks?

Yeah, I suppose so. Um... sometimes I'll send out a clinic staffing schedule, or... an email for the soccer league, thinking I checked it. But then someone points out I put the wrong date, or left off a location. Just... little details I missed that I would've caught before. So, yeah.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're sitting still?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think I have an issue with sitting still.
Do you often feel guilty or worthless about not getting your work done?
Um... no. I wouldn't say that. I mean, it's frustrating when things pile up, but... I don't really feel worthless. It's just work.
Do you often worry about things in your daily life?
Um... no. Not especially. I mean, there's always stuff to deal with, but... I don't really sit around worrying about it.
Do you often feel tired or lacking in energy?
Not particularly. I mean... I have enough energy to get through the day. My energy levels are fine.
Have you experienced any extremely stressful or traumatic events in your life?
No. Um... nothing like that. Just the usual day-to-day stress, I guess. Nothing I'd call traumatic.
How long have you been having trouble with sitting-down brain work?

Um... almost two years. Maybe a year and eleven months, I guess. That's... well, a friend of mine died around then. I ended up having to take on more of the, uh, league and outreach responsibilities after that. So... yeah. Since then.
Did your trouble with sitting-down brain work start around the same time your friend died?
Yeah. I mean... I suppose it was around then. The timing lines up, anyway.
Do you often think about your friend who died?
Um... no. Not really. I mean... I try not to dwell on it. Just... try to stay focused on work, mostly.
Do you ever find yourself thinking about your friend who died when you're not trying to?
No. I... I don't really think about it. I just try to keep busy.
Have you felt a persistent sense of sadness or emptiness since your friend died?
No, not really. I mean... I wouldn't say that. I just... I go to work, come home. It's just normal life.
Have you noticed any changes in your motivation to do things you normally enjoy?
No... not really. I mean, I still do the same things I usually do. Haven't really noticed a change.
Have you noticed any significant difficulty in completing tasks or achieving your goals at work since you started having trouble with sitting-down brain work?

I mean... I'm still getting by, mostly. At work and, you know, outside of it. But... I guess some deadlines have slipped. People have had to step in and cover some gaps for me. I've had to make a lot of last-minute apologies to coworkers... and friends. It's... it's embarrassing. But I'm still working.
Have you ever felt a strong desire to avoid thinking about your friend who died, even when you're not actively trying to think about work or other tasks?
No, I don't think so. I just... I don't really think about it much.
Do you think avoiding these tasks makes you feel better emotionally?
I don't know. Not really. I don't... I don't really think about how it makes me feel. I just put them off.
Do you put off tasks because they feel overwhelming?
I guess... I don't know if "overwhelming" is the right word. I just... I just don't do them.
Do you think doing these tasks would make you feel worse emotionally if you actually did them?
I'm not sure. I mean... I don't think they'd make me feel worse. It's just getting started on them that's the problem. I don't really know why.
Do you think there's something specific that's causing you to put off these tasks, or is it just that you don't feel like doing them?
I don't think there's anything specific. I just... I guess I just don't feel like doing them. I don't really have a good reason.
